issues: Max IOB of 25 U and Max Basal of 12 U/h are exceptionally high for a user with a Total Daily Insulin of approximately 20 U/day, removing automated safety guardrails.
Severe hypoglycemia is clustered in the evening and overnight (19:00, 00:00-02:00) with multiple extreme low readings reaching 41-45 mg/dL.
The 10-hour Duration of Insulin Action (DIA) causes the system to track insulin long after its typical peak, overlapping with trailing overnight automation.
The nighttime target of 90 mg/dL provides zero safety buffer against minor basal or UAM over-delivery.
Complete reliance on Unannounced Meals (UAM) without carb logging forces the system into a continuous reactive state to chase post-prandial rises.
summary: The data shows excellent CGM coverage but reveals a highly reactive, unannounced meal strategy (UAM) without appropriate automation limits. The AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal settings are disproportionately high for the user's total daily insulin. When chasing unannounced meals, this lack of constraints allows the system to over-deliver insulin. Combined with a 10-hour DIA and an aggressive 90 mg/dL overnight target, this mechanical stacking is the primary driver of severe, recurring evening and overnight hypoglycemia.
education: Max IOB and Max Basal act as the final safety nets in an automated loop. Setting them significantly higher than your actual daily needs allows the system to deliver excessive insulin when chasing unannounced glucose spikes.

A 10-hour DIA instructs the algorithm that insulin remains active and lowering glucose for 10 hours. While some dilute insulins or GLP-1 interactions alter timing, overstating DIA can lead to stacked corrections.

Unannounced meals (UAM) force the pump to react to glucose that has already risen. Without carb announcements, the pump cannot safely pre-calculate the required insulin, leading to trailing high doses.
strengths: Excellent CGM data coverage (98.7%) with very few gaps provides a reliable foundation for loop decisions.
Highly stable glucose and excellent Time in Range (95-98%) during the morning fasting window (04:00-09:00).
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
The severe lows (41-45 mg/dL) require immediate attention to maximum insulin delivery limits (Max IOB and Max Basal).
Do not change profile settings (Basal, Target, CR, ISF, DIA) at the same time as automation safety limits to avoid compounding variables.

analysis_steps.evidence: 14 days of data, 98.7% CGM coverage, 10 minor gaps. 2315 total treatments with 655 insulin entries. Exactly 0 carb entries logged.
analysis_steps.findings: Telemetry and CGM coverage are excellent. However, there are absolutely no carbs logged in the 14-day period. This indicates reliance entirely on unannounced meals (UAM) and AAPS automation for meal handling.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Total absence of meal size, composition, and timing data.

analysis_steps.evidence: Overall TBR is 5.1%. TBR is heavily clustered: 19:00 (15.3%), 23:00 (10.1%), 00:00 (11.4%), 01:00 (18.5%), and 02:00 (10.1%). Multiple low extremes (41-45 mg/dL).
analysis_steps.findings: There is a severe, recurring safety risk of evening and overnight hypoglycemia. Mitigating these nighttime lows is the absolute priority constraint.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: It is unclear if evening lows are purely basal-driven or the tail end of aggressive UAM corrections from dinner.

analysis_steps.evidence: Nighttime targets are set to 90 mg/dL. Morning (04:00-09:00) has near 0% TBR. Evening/Night has >10% TBR.
analysis_steps.findings: The overnight target of 90 mg/dL provides zero buffer against automation overshoots. Morning basal rates hold well, but the target creates unnecessary vulnerability overnight.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Cannot securely isolate pure fasting periods due to UAM for all meals.

analysis_steps.evidence: DIA is 10 hours. Flat ISF at 56 mg/dL/U. CR varies (10.5-13.2). Zero carbs logged.
analysis_steps.findings: The 10-hour DIA heavily extends the system's assumption of insulin action, which stacks with trailing UAM corrections and drives evening glucose low. CR is effectively bypassed without carb logging.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: CR validity cannot be assessed without carb logging.

analysis_steps.evidence: smb_enabled=true, uam_enabled=true, smb_interval_minutes=3. Zero announced carbs.
analysis_steps.findings: The system acts as a pure closed-loop reactive UAM setup. A 3-minute SMB interval allows rapid stacking of insulin at the first sign of a glucose rise.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: User's intent (deliberate no-carb strategy vs omission) is unconfirmed.

analysis_steps.evidence: max_basal_u_per_hour=12 (15x highest basal), max_iob_units=25. TDI is ~19.7 U/day.
analysis_steps.findings: There is a severe safety mismatch. A max_iob of 25 U exceeds the user's entire daily insulin requirement. This mechanical lack of constraints allows UAM to dangerously over-deliver.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Peak IOB reached during actual low events must be inferred from the crashes.

analysis_steps.evidence: 0 carb entries, 0 prebolus records, empty meal_strategies in analysis_context.
analysis_steps.findings: The execution strategy is 100% reliance on AAPS UAM and rapid SMBs. All post-prandial control is delegated to the pump, which over-delivers due to missing safety limits.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Total lack of declared or observed carbohydrate intake and meal timing.

analysis_steps.findings: Without carb entries, e-carbs and absorption patterns cannot be evaluated.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Zero standard or e-carb entries to evaluate.

analysis_steps.evidence: TDI ~20U, Max IOB 25U, severe overnight lows, 0 logged carbs.
analysis_steps.findings: The primary cause of the severe hypoglycemia is unconstrained UAM automation. The system chases unannounced meals with massive safety limits and a 10h DIA, resulting in delayed crashes. Tightening Max IOB and Max Basal is the paramount safety intervention.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Underlying profile accuracy cannot be verified until automation limits are constrained.

recommendations.title: Tighten Max IOB and Max Basal limits
recommendations.description: Current limits allow AAPS to deliver more insulin at once than is required for a full day, causing severe UAM over-corrections.

recommendations.title: Review 10-hour DIA
recommendations.description: A 10-hour DIA tracks insulin for much longer than rapid insulin typically acts, leading to miscalculated trailing corrections. Review if this was declared intentionally for a non-standard insulin type.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits allow dangerous insulin over-delivery given the user's ~20U TDI. Tightening these creates an essential guardrail.

implementation_steps: Dramatically reduce Max IOB and Max Basal in AAPS to protect against runaway UAM over-delivery.
Monitor evening and overnight glucose to verify if the severe lows (41-45 mg/dL) are mitigated by the new safety limits.
Review the 10-hour DIA with the care team to confirm if it accurately reflects the prescribed insulin action time.
Consider entering carbs for 1-2 daily meals to assess whether predictive COB bolusing provides smoother control than reactive UAM.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies 100% on unannounced meals (UAM) and frequent SMBs to control post-prandial glucose. Without safety limits, this aggressive automation causes severe delayed hypoglycemia.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Ensure Max IOB and Max Basal are safely capped so that unannounced meals do not trigger massive insulin stacking.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log carbohydrates for 2-3 typical meals to evaluate underlying CR and ISF validity and to observe if announced meals reduce delayed nighttime lows.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Profile settings (basal, CR, ISF, DIA, targets) should remain static until the severe safety mismatch in AAPS Max IOB and Max Basal limits is resolved, preventing simultaneous dependent changes.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight Time Below Range after AAPS safety limits are tightened to determine if profile basal rates or targets also require adjustment.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep profile settings unchanged and prioritize tightening AAPS safety limits.
